result.title: Operator-Valued Q-Learning: Compositional Bellman Recursions for Order-Sensitive Decision Making
result.summary: In quantum pulse sequences, spacecraft attitude control and in-hand reorientation, actions act on a hidden physical state as non-commuting operators, so the outcome of a plan depends on the order of its actions. We let the value function carry this structure: each Q(s,a) is an N x N operator, and the Bellman backup applies the action's dual map to the continuation value, Q(s,a) = K_a^*(R(s,a) + gamma E V(s')). Unrolled along a plan, the recursion builds the ordered product of the actions' operators, and the value at any latent state is a linear trace readout. It is exact for policies that do not observe the latent, the backup contracts for unitary and orthogonal dynamics, and an asynchronous operator TD scheme learns it with almost-sure convergence. Classical values live in a lattice, so a maximum over actions exists; self-adjoint operators form an anti-lattice (Kadison) and have none. An operator log-sum-exp still gives one operator per state-action pair whose readout upper-bounds the value of every policy at every latent state. The sampled update converges to it for a finite horizon, and it reduces to soft Q-learning and the QMDP bound when actions commute. We prove that scalar values on observations that ignore action order must confuse swapped histories, that exact history tables grow exponentially for free action groups but polynomially for nilpotent ones, and give a Hankel-rank lower bound on the operator dimension. In experiments the learned policy matches 1000-simulation tree search on SO(3) pointing for horizons up to 20 at ~10^4 times lower decision cost, transfers zero-shot to unseen initial states, and acts exactly on its belief mean when the initial state is hidden, where plugging the mean into a DQN does not. A planner with the same model knowledge is more sample-efficient at short horizons, and a DQN given the operators matches or exceeds OpQ.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 operator-valued Q-learning：把 Q(s,a) 设为 N×N 算子，Bellman 备份通过动作的对偶映射作用，沿计划展开得到算子的有序乘积，并以迹读出得到 latent 状态上的值；同时给出反格结构、算子 log-sum-exp 上界、历史表增长率与 Hankel 秩下界等理论，并在 SO(3) 指向任务上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 非交换算子复合与「顺序敏感」可类比 latent 推理步骤的复合次序问题；其「忽略动作顺序的标量值必然混淆交换后的历史」这一负结果，可能为 latent 状态压缩与信息坍缩的诊断及读出维度下界提供核查线索。
